name: Question 15
worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int (3-4x)^{2/3}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we let  $u=3-4x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $u$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3-4x)^{2/3}\,\text{d}x & =\int {u}^{2/3}\cdot (-\frac{1}{4})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\int {u}^{2/3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{5/3}{u}^{5/3}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{3}{5}{u}^{5/3}+C \\  & =-\frac{3}{20}{u}^{5/3}+C \\  & =-\frac{3}{20}(3-4x)^{5/3}+C \\  & =-\frac{3}{20}\sqrt[3]{(3-4x)^{5}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[-\frac{3}{20}(3-4x)^{5/3}+C] & =-\frac{3}{20}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(3-4x)^{5/3}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =-\frac{3}{20}\cdot \frac{5}{3}(3-4x)^{2/3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3-4x)+0 \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(3-4x)^{3/2}\cdot (-4) \\  & =(3-4x)^{3/2} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{(3-4x)^{2}}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Calculate the integral ∫(3−4x)23dx.

a
−320(3−4x)23+C
b
−320(3−4x)53+C
c
−35(3−4x)53+C
d
−15(3−4x)23+C
e
−15(3−4x)53+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we rewrite the integral as

∫(3−4x)2/3dx.

Now, we let u=3−4x. Then differentiating with respect to x gives

dudx=−4⟹dx=−14du.

We now write our integral in terms of u, calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of u at the very end:

∫(3−4x)2/3dx=∫u2/3⋅(−14)du=−14∫u2/3du=−14⋅15/3u5/3+C=−14⋅35u5/3+C=−320u5/3+C=−320(3−4x)5/3+C=−320(3−4x)53+C

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

ddx[−320(3−4x)5/3+C]=−320⋅ddx[(3−4x)5/3]+ddx(C)=−320⋅53(3−4x)2/3⋅ddx(3−4x)+0=−14(3−4x)3/2⋅(−4)=(3−4x)3/2=(3−4x)23✓
